docs.text: The rest of src/btree.cpp (below); the remaining tests in tests/btree_test.cpp, and the fixture's erase helper.

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
src/btree.cpp, the two functions between insert and check:

bool BPlusTree::erase(std::string_view key) {
    PageCache::PageRef ref = cache_.fetch(find_leaf(key));
    LeafNode leaf = decode_leaf(ref.read());
    const auto it = leaf_lower_bound(leaf, key);
    if (it == leaf.cells.end() || it->first != key) {
        return false;
    }
    leaf.cells.erase(it);
    encode_leaf(leaf, ref.write());  // no merge: see the class comment
    return true;
}

std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> BPlusTree::scan(std::string_view start, std::string_view end,
                                                                 std::size_t limit) {
    std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> out;
    if (limit == 0) {
        return out;
    }
    std::uint32_t page_count = 0;
    {
        PageCache::PageRef meta_ref = cache_.fetch(kMetaPageId);
        page_count = Meta::decode(meta_ref.read()).page_count;
    }
    PageId id = find_leaf(start);
    for (std::uint32_t hops = 0; id != kNoPage; ++hops) {
        if (hops > page_count) {
            throw CorruptionError("leaf chain longer than the file (cycle?)");
        }
        PageCache::PageRef ref = cache_.fetch(id);
        LeafNode leaf = decode_leaf(ref.read());
        for (auto& [key, value] : leaf.cells) {
            if (std::string_view(key).compare(start) < 0) {
                continue;
            }
            if (!end.empty() && std::string_view(key).compare(end) >= 0) {
                return out;
            }
            out.emplace_back(std::move(key), std::move(value));
            if (out.size() >= limit) {
                return out;
            }
        }
        id = leaf.next;
    }
    return out;
}

scan refuses to follow more leaf links than there are pages in the file: a corrupted next_leaf that points backwards would otherwise loop forever.

TEST_F(TreeFixture, EmptyTree) {
    EXPECT_FALSE(tree_.get("x").has_value());
    EXPECT_TRUE(tree_.scan("", "", 10).empty());
    EXPECT_EQ(tree_.check(), 0u);
}

TEST_F(TreeFixture, SequentialInsertsSplitLeavesAndInternals) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 5000; ++i) {
        put(key_of(i), std::string(400, 'v'));  // ~9 cells per leaf: hundreds of leaves
    }
    EXPECT_EQ(tree_.check(), 5000u);
    EXPECT_EQ(tree_.get(key_of(4321)).value_or("").size(), 400u);
    const auto range = tree_.scan(key_of(10), key_of(20), 100);
    ASSERT_EQ(range.size(), 10u);
    EXPECT_EQ(range.front().first, key_of(10));
}

TEST_F(TreeFixture, MatchesStdMapUnderRandomOperations) {
    std::map<std::string, std::string> model;
    std::mt19937 rng(7);
    for (int step = 0; step < 40000; ++step) {
        const std::string key = key_of(static_cast<int>(rng() % 4000));
        if (rng() % 3 != 0) {
            const std::string value(rng() % (kMaxValueSize + 1), static_cast<char>('a' + rng() % 26));
            put(key, value);
            model[key] = value;
        } else {
            EXPECT_EQ(erase(key), model.erase(key) == 1);
        }
        if (step % 5000 == 0) {
            ASSERT_EQ(tree_.check(), model.size());
        }
    }
    ASSERT_EQ(tree_.check(), model.size());
    const auto all = tree_.scan("", "", SIZE_MAX);
    ASSERT_EQ(all.size(), model.size());
    auto it = model.begin();
    for (const auto& [k, v] : all) {
        ASSERT_EQ(k, it->first);
        ASSERT_EQ(v, it->second);
        ++it;
    }
}

Forty thousand operations over 4,000 keys with values up to the maximum size: hundreds of splits, thousands of deletes, empty leaves, and a check every 5,000 steps. The fixed seed (7) makes a failure reproducible; when one fails, print step and shrink the loop until the smallest failing sequence remains.

docs.title: Step 6. Wal: records, LSNs, sync, replay, truncate, reset
docs.text: Time: ~6 hours Week: 8 Read first: 07_Databases_Internals/04_wal_and_crash_recovery.md (all of it). 06_Linux_Toolchain_DevOps/07_debugging_and_profiling_tools_on_linux.md (strace -e trace=fdatasync,pwrite64 to see the commit protocol happen).

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
The write-ahead log: append page-image and commit records, make them durable with one fdatasync, read them back after a crash stopping cleanly at a torn tail, cut the log at a chosen point, and replace it with an empty one at a checkpoint without ever losing the LSN sequence.

In plain words: the receipt pad from 00_spec.md section 1. Every receipt is numbered by its position on an endless roll of paper (the LSN), sealed (CRC), and the roll is only considered "in the safe" after fdatasync returns.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• LSN = byte position in a logical log that never restarts: start_lsn + (offset - 24). The record stores its own LSN, so replay can tell a record written here from leftover bytes of an earlier, longer log.
  • Append buffers, sync() writes and syncs. One pwrite and one fdatasync per commit, however many records the transaction has. ensure_durable(lsn) is what the cache's WAL hook calls: it syncs only if that LSN is not durable yet.
  • Replay stops at the first invalid record: incomplete, wrong length for its type, LSN not equal to its position, or CRC mismatch. All of those mean "the crash happened here".
  • truncate_at is separate from replay. Recovery decides where the log ends: just after the last commit, not just after the last valid record. The first draft of this code truncated after the last valid record; Recovery.UncommittedTailIsDiscardedAndNotReplayedLater (step 7) failed, because the page images of a crashed transaction stayed in the log, in front of the next transaction's records, and the next recovery applied them as part of that transaction's commit. Keep that story: it is a real ordering bug, and a test you wrote found it.
  • reset() never rewrites the header in place. It builds <path>.tmp with a header whose start_lsn is the current end, syncs it, renames it over the log, syncs the directory. A crash leaves the old log (replaying it is harmless after a checkpoint) or the new empty one.
  • LSN 0 is reserved, a new log starts at kFirstLsn = 1. Why is in step 7.

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <functional>
#include <string>

#include "minidb/file.hpp"
#include "minidb/page.hpp"

namespace minidb {

enum class RecordType : std::uint8_t { PageImage = 1, Commit = 2 };

struct WalRecord {
    Lsn lsn = 0;
    RecordType type = RecordType::Commit;
    PageId page_id = 0;        // PageImage
    std::uint64_t txn_id = 0;  // Commit
    Page image;                // PageImage: the full page after the change, sealed
};

// Write-ahead log: an append-only file next to the data file ("<db>-wal").
//
// File layout:
//   header (24 bytes): u64 magic | u64 start_lsn | u32 crc32(first 16 bytes) | u32 zero
//   records, back to back:
//     u32 crc32(bytes [4, 24) + payload) | u32 payload_len | u64 lsn | u8 type | 3 x u8 zero |
//     u32 page_id | payload (4096-byte page image, or u64 txn id for Commit)
//
// LSN = start_lsn + (file offset - header size). LSNs only grow: reset() starts the next log
// at the current end LSN, so a page LSN can be compared with any record LSN.
//
// The header is never rewritten in place. A new log (creation or reset) is built as
// "<path>.tmp", fsynced, and renamed over the old one, so the file always has a valid header
// and either the old records or none.
//
// Durability: append_*() only buffer in memory; sync() writes the buffer and fdatasyncs.
// A record is durable once durable_lsn() is greater than its LSN.
class Wal {
public:
    // LSN 0 is reserved: it is the LSN of pages that were never logged (written by
    // Pager::create). If the first record also had LSN 0, recovery would see a page with
    // LSN 0 >= record LSN 0 and wrongly skip the redo.
    static constexpr Lsn kFirstLsn = 1;

    // Opens the log at `path`, creating an empty one (start LSN kFirstLsn) if it does not exist.
    // Throws CorruptionError if an existing file has an invalid header.
    explicit Wal(const std::string& path);
    Wal(const Wal&) = delete;
    Wal& operator=(const Wal&) = delete;

    // Recovery: calls `fn` for every valid record in order, stopping at the first record that
    // is incomplete, has a bad checksum or an unexpected LSN: the torn tail of a crash.
    // Returns the number of valid records. Does not modify the file.
    std::size_t replay(const std::function<void(const WalRecord&)>& fn);

    // Recovery: discard everything from `end` onwards (the records of a transaction that never
    // committed, and any torn tail). Must be called before the first append after replay(),
    // or those orphaned page images would be mistaken for part of the next transaction.
    void truncate_at(Lsn end);

    // Stamps the page with the record's LSN, seals it, and buffers the record.
    Lsn append_page(PageId id, Page& page);
    Lsn append_commit(std::uint64_t txn_id);

    void sync();                     // write buffered records, then fdatasync
    void ensure_durable(Lsn lsn);    // sync() unless the record at `lsn` is already durable
    void discard_buffer() noexcept;  // drop unsynced records (a transaction that failed)

    // Checkpoint: the data file has been synced and contains every logged change. Replace
    // the log with an empty one that starts at end_lsn().
    void reset();

    Lsn start_lsn() const noexcept { return start_lsn_; }
    Lsn end_lsn() const noexcept { return end_lsn_; }          // LSN the next record gets
    Lsn durable_lsn() const noexcept { return durable_lsn_; }  // everything below is on disk
    std::uint64_t size_bytes() const noexcept { return kHeaderSize + (end_lsn_ - start_lsn_); }

    static constexpr std::size_t kHeaderSize = 24;
    static constexpr std::size_t kRecordHeaderSize = 24;

private:
    static void create_empty(const std::string& path, Lsn start_lsn);
    std::uint64_t offset_of(Lsn lsn) const noexcept { return kHeaderSize + (lsn - start_lsn_); }

    std::string path_;
    File file_;
    Lsn start_lsn_ = 0;
    Lsn end_lsn_ = 0;
    Lsn durable_lsn_ = 0;
    std::string buffer_;  // encoded records in [durable_lsn_, end_lsn_)
};

}  // namespace minidb

#include "minidb/wal.hpp"

#include <array>

#include "minidb/crc32.hpp"

namespace minidb {

namespace {

constexpr std::uint64_t kWalMagic = 0x314C41574244494DULL;  // arbitrary, fixed forever

std::uint32_t payload_size(RecordType type) noexcept {
    return type == RecordType::PageImage ? static_cast<std::uint32_t>(kPageSize) : 8u;
}

void encode_record(std::string& out, Lsn lsn, RecordType type, PageId page_id, const char* payload,
                   std::uint32_t payload_len) {
    std::array<char, Wal::kRecordHeaderSize> header{};
    write_as(header.data() + 4, payload_len);
    write_as(header.data() + 8, lsn);
    write_as(header.data() + 16, static_cast<std::uint8_t>(type));
    write_as(header.data() + 20, page_id);
    std::uint32_t crc = crc32(header.data() + 4, header.size() - 4);
    crc = crc32(payload, payload_len, crc);
    write_as(header.data(), crc);
    out.append(header.data(), header.size());
    out.append(payload, payload_len);
}

}  // namespace

void Wal::create_empty(const std::string& path, Lsn start_lsn) {
    std::array<char, kHeaderSize> header{};
    write_as(header.data(), kWalMagic);
    write_as(header.data() + 8, start_lsn);
    write_as(header.data() + 16, crc32(header.data(), 16));

    const std::string tmp = path + ".tmp";
    {
        File file = File::open(tmp, /*create=*/true);
        file.truncate(0);
        file.write_at(0, header.data(), header.size());
        file.sync();
    }
    rename_file(tmp, path);         // atomic: readers see the old log or the new one
    sync_parent_directory(path);    // and the rename survives a power cut
}

Wal::Wal(const std::string& path) : path_(path) {
    if (!file_exists(path)) {
        create_empty(path, kFirstLsn);
    }
    file_ = File::open(path, /*create=*/false);

    std::array<char, kHeaderSize> header{};
    const std::size_t n = file_.read_at(0, header.data(), header.size());
    if (n != kHeaderSize || read_as<std::uint64_t>(header.data()) != kWalMagic ||
        read_as<std::uint32_t>(header.data() + 16) != crc32(header.data(), 16)) {
        throw CorruptionError("WAL " + path + ": invalid header");
    }
    start_lsn_ = read_as<Lsn>(header.data() + 8);
    end_lsn_ = start_lsn_;
    durable_lsn_ = start_lsn_;
}

std::size_t Wal::replay(const std::function<void(const WalRecord&)>& fn) {
    std::size_t count = 0;
    Lsn lsn = start_lsn_;
    WalRecord record;
    std::array<char, kRecordHeaderSize> header{};
    std::array<char, 8> commit_payload{};
    for (;;) {
        const std::uint64_t offset = offset_of(lsn);
        if (file_.read_at(offset, header.data(), header.size()) != header.size()) {
            break;  // clean end of log, or a torn record header
        }
        const auto len = read_as<std::uint32_t>(header.data() + 4);
        const auto type = static_cast<RecordType>(read_as<std::uint8_t>(header.data() + 16));
        if ((type != RecordType::PageImage && type != RecordType::Commit) || len != payload_size(type) ||
            read_as<Lsn>(header.data() + 8) != lsn) {
            break;  // garbage: not a record we wrote at this position
        }
        char* payload = type == RecordType::PageImage ? record.image.bytes.data() : commit_payload.data();
        if (file_.read_at(offset + kRecordHeaderSize, payload, len) != len) {
            break;  // torn payload
        }
        std::uint32_t crc = crc32(header.data() + 4, header.size() - 4);
        crc = crc32(payload, len, crc);
        if (crc != read_as<std::uint32_t>(header.data())) {
            break;  // torn or corrupted record
        }
        record.lsn = lsn;
        record.type = type;
        record.page_id = read_as<PageId>(header.data() + 20);
        record.txn_id = type == RecordType::Commit ? read_as<std::uint64_t>(commit_payload.data()) : 0;
        fn(record);
        ++count;
        lsn += kRecordHeaderSize + len;
    }
    return count;
}

void Wal::truncate_at(Lsn end) {
    if (end < start_lsn_) {
        throw DbError("WAL truncate_at: LSN before start of log");
    }
    // Cut the uncommitted or torn tail so new records follow the last commit directly.
    // Otherwise a later replay would see the orphaned images, or stop at the old garbage
    // before reaching newer committed records.
    file_.truncate(offset_of(end));
    file_.sync();
    buffer_.clear();
    end_lsn_ = end;
    durable_lsn_ = end;
}

Lsn Wal::append_page(PageId id, Page& page) {
    const Lsn lsn = end_lsn_;
    page.set_lsn(lsn);
    page.seal();
    encode_record(buffer_, lsn, RecordType::PageImage, id, page.bytes.data(),
                  static_cast<std::uint32_t>(kPageSize));
    end_lsn_ += kRecordHeaderSize + kPageSize;
    return lsn;
}

Lsn Wal::append_commit(std::uint64_t txn_id) {
    const Lsn lsn = end_lsn_;
    std::array<char, 8> payload{};
    write_as(payload.data(), txn_id);
    encode_record(buffer_, lsn, RecordType::Commit, 0, payload.data(), 8);
    end_lsn_ += kRecordHeaderSize + 8;
    return lsn;
}

void Wal::sync() {
    if (!buffer_.empty()) {
        file_.write_at(offset_of(durable_lsn_), buffer_.data(), buffer_.size());
    }
    file_.sync();
    durable_lsn_ = end_lsn_;
    buffer_.clear();
}

void Wal::ensure_durable(Lsn lsn) {
    if (lsn >= durable_lsn_) {
        sync();
    }
}

void Wal::discard_buffer() noexcept {
    buffer_.clear();
    end_lsn_ = durable_lsn_;
}

void Wal::reset() {
    if (!buffer_.empty()) {
        sync();
    }
    file_ = File();  // close before replacing the file
    create_empty(path_, end_lsn_);
    file_ = File::open(path_, /*create=*/false);
    start_lsn_ = end_lsn_;
    durable_lsn_ = end_lsn_;
}

}  // namespace minidb

Notes:

  • The CRC covers the record header after the CRC field plus the payload, chained with the previous parameter of crc32: one checksum over two buffers without concatenating them.
  • discard_buffer() is for a transaction that failed before its records reached the file. The next sync() writes at the durable offset, overwriting whatever a failed attempt may have left there.
  • size_bytes() is what the Db compares with checkpoint_wal_bytes.

TEST(Wal, AppendSyncReplay) {
    TempDir dir;
    const std::string path = dir.file("wal");
    Lsn first = 0;
    {
        Wal wal(path);
        wal.truncate_at(wal.start_lsn());
        Page page = page_with_byte('q');
        first = wal.append_page(7, page);
        EXPECT_EQ(page.lsn(), first);  // the page carries its record's LSN
        wal.append_commit(1);
        wal.sync();
        EXPECT_EQ(wal.durable_lsn(), wal.end_lsn());
    }
    Wal wal(path);
    std::vector<WalRecord> seen;
    EXPECT_EQ(wal.replay([&](const WalRecord& r) { seen.push_back(r); }), 2u);
    ASSERT_EQ(seen.size(), 2u);
    EXPECT_EQ(seen[0].type, RecordType::PageImage);
    EXPECT_EQ(seen[0].page_id, 7u);
    EXPECT_EQ(seen[0].lsn, first);
    EXPECT_TRUE(seen[0].image.verify());
    EXPECT_EQ(seen[1].type, RecordType::Commit);
    EXPECT_EQ(seen[1].txn_id, 1u);
}

TEST(Wal, TornTailIsIgnored) {
    TempDir dir;
    const std::string path = dir.file("wal");
    {
        Wal wal(path);
        Page page = page_with_byte('q');
        wal.append_page(1, page);
        wal.append_commit(1);
        wal.append_page(2, page);
        wal.append_commit(2);
        wal.sync();
    }
    {
        // Simulate a crash in the middle of writing the second transaction's page image.
        File f = File::open(path, false);
        f.truncate(Wal::kHeaderSize + (Wal::kRecordHeaderSize + kPageSize) + (Wal::kRecordHeaderSize + 8) + 1000);
    }
    Wal wal(path);
    std::size_t commits = 0;
    EXPECT_EQ(wal.replay([&](const WalRecord& r) { commits += r.type == RecordType::Commit ? 1 : 0; }), 2u);
    EXPECT_EQ(commits, 1u);
}

TEST(Wal, ResetKeepsLsnsMonotonic) {
    TempDir dir;
    const std::string path = dir.file("wal");
    Wal wal(path);
    Page page = page_with_byte('q');
    wal.append_page(1, page);
    wal.append_commit(1);
    wal.sync();
    const Lsn end = wal.end_lsn();
    wal.reset();
    EXPECT_EQ(wal.start_lsn(), end);
    EXPECT_EQ(wal.size_bytes(), Wal::kHeaderSize);
    EXPECT_EQ(wal.append_commit(2), end);  // the next record continues the sequence
}

docs.title: What to say in an interview
docs.text: "The log is append-only and each record carries a CRC and its own LSN, which is its byte position in a logical log that never restarts, so replay can tell the torn tail of a crash from valid records. A commit is one pwrite and one fdatasync of everything the transaction appended. Two details I got wrong first and my tests caught: after a crash the log must be cut after the last commit, not the last valid record, or a crashed transaction's page images get replayed as part of the next commit; and LSN 0 must be reserved for pages that were never logged."

docs.title: Step 7. Recovery and Db: the commit protocol and checkpoints
docs.text: Time: ~8 hours Week: 9 Read first: 07_Databases_Internals/04_wal_and_crash_recovery.md again (ARIES: analysis, redo, undo; steal/no-steal, force/no-force), 05_transactions_acid_mvcc.md (atomicity and durability). 04_Concurrency/03_mutexes_lock_guard_unique_lock.md. 02_Modern_CPP: 10_error_handling_exceptions_optional_expected.md (exception safety: the strong guarantee).

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Wire everything into the public Db class: transactions around every put and del, the commit protocol, checkpoints, and redo-only crash recovery on open. After this step the durability contract in 00_spec.md section 2 holds.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
The commit protocol, in the order that makes it crash-safe (Db::commit):

1. for every page in the transaction: Wal::append_page   (stamps the page LSN, seals it)
2. Wal::append_commit
3. Wal::sync()                 <-- durable from here; the call may now return
4. PageCache::commit_txn()     pages become ordinary dirty pages, evictable

The data file is not touched at commit (no-force). It catches up at eviction (after the WAL hook) or at a checkpoint.

  • Strong exception guarantee for put/del. write_txn runs the tree operation and the commit; if anything throws, abort_txn() restores every before-image and discard_buffer() forgets the buffered records. The database is exactly as it was before the call.
  • A failed fdatasync poisons the Db. After a failed fsync the kernel may have dropped the dirty pages and cleared the error, so retrying can falsely succeed (PostgreSQL's 2018 "fsyncgate"). The only safe response is to refuse further operations and let recovery decide on the next open.
  • Checkpoint = flush_all(), Pager::sync(), Wal::reset(). Run when the log passes checkpoint_wal_bytes, on open after recovery, and in the destructor.
  • Recovery (00_spec.md section 7): replay, collect page images per transaction, apply them at the commit record, skip pages whose LSN shows they are already current, discard the uncommitted tail, sync the data file, cut the log after the last commit.
  • The LSN-0 bug. In the first draft the log started at LSN 0. A freshly created database has page 1 (the root leaf) with page LSN 0. The first put logged page 1 at LSN 0. After a crash, recovery compared the data file's page LSN (0) with the record's (0), concluded "already current", and skipped the redo: the first committed write of every database was lost if the process died before a checkpoint. The SIGKILL crash test did not catch it (by the time it kills, page 1 has been logged many times at higher LSNs); the deterministic test below did. The fix is one constant: logs start at LSN 1, and LSN 0 means "never logged".
  • Member order is construction order. Pager, then Wal, then RecoveryStats (whose initialiser runs recovery), then the cache and the tree. Recovery must finish before the cache reads its first page. The constructor initialiser list makes that ordering explicit and impossible to get wrong later.

docs.text:
#pragma once

#include <cstddef>

#include "minidb/pager.hpp"
#include "minidb/wal.hpp"

namespace minidb {

struct RecoveryStats {
    std::size_t records = 0;              // valid records found in the log
    std::size_t committed_txns = 0;       // transactions with a commit record
    std::size_t pages_redone = 0;         // page images written to the data file
    std::size_t pages_skipped = 0;        // data file already had this image or a newer one
    std::size_t discarded_records = 0;    // records of a transaction that never committed
    Lsn end_lsn = 0;                      // log end after recovery (just past the last commit)
};

// Redo-only crash recovery.
//
// Why redo-only works: the PageCache never writes a page modified by an uncommitted
// transaction to the data file (no-steal), so the data file never needs undoing. It may,
// however, be missing committed changes (no-force: commit only syncs the log) and may hold a
// torn page (crash during a page write). Every committed change is in the log as a full page
// image, so replaying committed images in log order repairs both.
//
// Idempotent: running it twice, or crashing during it and running it again, gives the same
// result, because applying a full page image is idempotent and replay is in LSN order.
class Recovery {
public:
    static RecoveryStats run(Pager& pager, Wal& wal);
};

}  // namespace minidb

#include "minidb/recovery.hpp"

#include <utility>
#include <vector>

namespace minidb {

RecoveryStats Recovery::run(Pager& pager, Wal& wal) {
    RecoveryStats stats;
    stats.end_lsn = wal.start_lsn();

    // Page images of the transaction being read; applied only when its commit record shows
    // up. Images of a transaction whose commit never reached the disk are never applied.
    std::vector<std::pair<PageId, Page>> pending;
    Page current;

    stats.records = wal.replay([&](const WalRecord& record) {
        if (record.type == RecordType::PageImage) {
            pending.emplace_back(record.page_id, record.image);
            return;
        }
        // Commit: redo every image of this transaction, in log order.
        for (auto& [page_id, image] : pending) {
            // The page LSN check is an optimisation, not a correctness requirement: if the
            // data file already holds this image or a later one, rewriting is unnecessary.
            // A torn or missing page fails read_if_valid() and is always rewritten.
            if (pager.read_if_valid(page_id, current) && current.lsn() >= image.lsn()) {
                ++stats.pages_skipped;
                continue;
            }
            pager.write(page_id, image);
            ++stats.pages_redone;
        }
        pending.clear();
        ++stats.committed_txns;
        stats.end_lsn = record.lsn + Wal::kRecordHeaderSize + 8;  // just past the commit record
    });

    stats.discarded_records = pending.size();
    pager.sync();                  // redone pages durable before the log can be reset
    wal.truncate_at(stats.end_lsn);  // drop the uncommitted tail before anything is appended
    return stats;
}

}  // namespace minidb

#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <mutex>
#include <optional>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include "minidb/btree.hpp"
#include "minidb/page_cache.hpp"
#include "minidb/pager.hpp"
#include "minidb/recovery.hpp"
#include "minidb/wal.hpp"

namespace minidb {

struct Options {
    std::size_t cache_pages = 256;                    // 1 MiB of page cache
    std::uint64_t checkpoint_wal_bytes = 8u << 20;    // checkpoint when the log passes 8 MiB
};

// The public API. Every put/del is its own transaction and is durable when the call returns:
// its WAL records have been fdatasynced. One mutex serialises all calls.
class Db {
public:
    // Opens `path` (and "<path>-wal"), creating both if the data file does not exist,
    // and runs crash recovery.
    explicit Db(const std::string& path, Options options = {});
    ~Db();  // checkpoints, so a clean shutdown leaves an empty log
    Db(const Db&) = delete;
    Db& operator=(const Db&) = delete;

    void put(std::string_view key, std::string_view value);
    std::optional<std::string> get(std::string_view key);
    bool del(std::string_view key);
    std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> scan(std::string_view start, std::string_view end = {},
                                                          std::size_t limit = SIZE_MAX);
    void checkpoint();
    std::size_t check();  // full structural check; returns key count

    const RecoveryStats& recovery_stats() const noexcept { return recovery_; }
    std::uint64_t wal_bytes() const noexcept { return wal_.size_bytes(); }
    const PageCache::Stats& cache_stats() const noexcept { return cache_.stats(); }

private:
    template <class F>
    auto write_txn(F&& body);
    void commit();
    void checkpoint_locked();
    void throw_if_failed() const;

    std::mutex mutex_;
    Options options_;
    Pager pager_;           // declaration order is construction order:
    Wal wal_;               // the log must exist before recovery,
    RecoveryStats recovery_;  // recovery must finish before the cache reads any page
    PageCache cache_;
    BPlusTree tree_;
    std::uint64_t next_txn_id_ = 1;
    bool failed_ = false;   // set when a commit fails part-way; see commit()
};

}  // namespace minidb

#include "minidb/db.hpp"

#include <stdexcept>

namespace minidb {

namespace {

// Runs before the Pager member is constructed: makes sure a data file exists.
const std::string& ensure_database(const std::string& path) {
    if (!file_exists(path)) {
        // A log left over from an older database with the same name must not be replayed
        // into the new one: replace it with an empty log first, then create the data file.
        if (file_exists(path + "-wal")) {
            rename_file(path + "-wal", path + "-wal.orphaned");
        }
        Pager::create(path, BPlusTree::initial_pages());
    }
    return path;
}

void validate(std::string_view key, std::string_view value) {
    if (key.empty() || key.size() > kMaxKeySize) {
        throw std::invalid_argument("minidb: key must be 1.." + std::to_string(kMaxKeySize) + " bytes");
    }
    if (value.size() > kMaxValueSize) {
        throw std::invalid_argument("minidb: value must be at most " + std::to_string(kMaxValueSize) + " bytes");
    }
}

}  // namespace

Db::Db(const std::string& path, Options options)
    : options_(options),
      pager_(ensure_database(path)),
      wal_(path + "-wal"),
      recovery_(Recovery::run(pager_, wal_)),
      cache_(pager_, options.cache_pages, [this](Lsn lsn) { wal_.ensure_durable(lsn); }),
      tree_(cache_) {
    {
        PageCache::PageRef meta = cache_.fetch(kMetaPageId);
        (void)Meta::decode(meta.read());  // throws CorruptionError for a non-minidb file
    }
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
    checkpoint_locked();  // fold the recovered log into the data file; start with an empty log
}

Db::~Db() {
    try {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
        if (!failed_) {
            checkpoint_locked();
        }
    } catch (...) {
        // Destructors must not throw. Nothing is lost: the log still holds every commit.
    }
}

void Db::throw_if_failed() const {
    if (failed_) {
        throw DbError("minidb: a previous commit failed; reopen the database to recover");
    }
}

template <class F>
auto Db::write_txn(F&& body) {
    throw_if_failed();
    try {
        auto result = body();
        commit();
        return result;
    } catch (...) {
        cache_.abort_txn();     // restore before-images: memory matches the last commit again
        wal_.discard_buffer();  // nothing of this transaction reaches the log
        throw;
    }
}

// The commit protocol, in the order that makes it crash-safe:
//   1. append a full image of every page this transaction changed (stamps page LSNs)
//   2. append a commit record
//   3. fdatasync the log                  <- the transaction is durable from here
//   4. release the pages to the cache as ordinary dirty pages (they may now be evicted)
// The data file is not touched. It catches up at eviction or checkpoint.
void Db::commit() {
    if (!cache_.in_txn()) {
        return;  // e.g. del() of a missing key changed nothing
    }
    cache_.for_each_txn_page([this](PageId id, Page& page) { wal_.append_page(id, page); });
    wal_.append_commit(next_txn_id_++);
    try {
        wal_.sync();
    } catch (...) {
        // fsync failed. The kernel may have dropped the dirty log pages, so we cannot know
        // what is on disk ("fsyncgate", PostgreSQL 2018). The only safe answer is to stop
        // accepting writes and let recovery decide on the next open.
        failed_ = true;
        throw;
    }
    cache_.commit_txn();
}

void Db::put(std::string_view key, std::string_view value) {
    validate(key, value);
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
    write_txn([&] {
        tree_.put(key, value);
        return true;
    });
    if (wal_.size_bytes() >= options_.checkpoint_wal_bytes) {
        checkpoint_locked();
    }
}

bool Db::del(std::string_view key) {
    if (key.empty() || key.size() > kMaxKeySize) {
        return false;
    }
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
    const bool removed = write_txn([&] { return tree_.erase(key); });
    if (wal_.size_bytes() >= options_.checkpoint_wal_bytes) {
        checkpoint_locked();
    }
    return removed;
}

std::optional<std::string> Db::get(std::string_view key) {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
    throw_if_failed();
    return tree_.get(key);
}

std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> Db::scan(std::string_view start, std::string_view end,
                                                          std::size_t limit) {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
    throw_if_failed();
    return tree_.scan(start, end, limit);
}

std::size_t Db::check() {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
    return tree_.check();
}

void Db::checkpoint() {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
    throw_if_failed();
    checkpoint_locked();
}

// Checkpoint: make the data file contain everything the log contains, then empty the log.
//   1. write every dirty page (each one's WAL record is already durable: the WAL rule)
//   2. fdatasync the data file
//   3. replace the log with an empty one starting at the current end LSN
// A crash before step 3 completes leaves the old log in place; replaying it is harmless.
void Db::checkpoint_locked() {
    cache_.flush_all();
    pager_.sync();
    wal_.reset();
}

}  // namespace minidb

ensure_database renames a log left behind by an older database of the same name instead of replaying it into the new one: without that, deleting the data file but not the log and then reopening would apply a stranger's page images to a fresh database. (A stronger version stores a random database id in both the meta page and the log header and refuses to replay on a mismatch; a good exercise.)

tests/db_test.cpp in full. The three Recovery tests simulate a crash by copying the data file and the log while the Db is still open (so its destructor's checkpoint has not run), then damaging the copy in a specific way:

// BPlusTree through the Db API, recovery, and a model-based property test against std::map.

#include <cstdio>
#include <filesystem>
#include <map>
#include <random>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include <gtest/gtest.h>

#include "minidb/db.hpp"
#include "test_util.hpp"

using namespace minidb;

namespace {

std::string key_of(int i) {
    char buf[16];
    std::snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, "k%08d", i);
    return buf;
}

}  // namespace

TEST(Db, PutGetDelOnFreshDatabase) {
    TempDir dir;
    Db db(dir.file("db"));
    EXPECT_FALSE(db.get("a").has_value());
    db.put("a", "1");
    db.put("b", "2");
    db.put("a", "3");  // overwrite
    EXPECT_EQ(db.get("a").value_or(""), "3");
    EXPECT_TRUE(db.del("a"));
    EXPECT_FALSE(db.del("a"));
    EXPECT_FALSE(db.get("a").has_value());
    EXPECT_EQ(db.check(), 1u);
}

TEST(Db, RejectsOversizedKeysAndValues) {
    TempDir dir;
    Db db(dir.file("db"));
    EXPECT_THROW(db.put("", "v"), std::invalid_argument);
    EXPECT_THROW(db.put(std::string(kMaxKeySize + 1, 'k'), "v"), std::invalid_argument);
    EXPECT_THROW(db.put("k", std::string(kMaxValueSize + 1, 'v')), std::invalid_argument);
    EXPECT_NO_THROW(db.put(std::string(kMaxKeySize, 'k'), std::string(kMaxValueSize, 'v')));
}

TEST(Db, ManySplitsKeepTheTreeValidAndScansOrdered) {
    TempDir dir;
    Db db(dir.file("db"), Options{32, 1u << 20});  // small cache: forces eviction and write-back
    constexpr int kCount = 6000;  // with 300..699-byte values: ~1,000 leaves, so internal nodes split too
    for (int i = 0; i < kCount; ++i) {
        const int k = (i * 7919) % kCount;  // a permutation: inserts arrive out of order
        db.put(key_of(k), std::string(static_cast<std::size_t>(300 + k % 400), 'v'));
    }
    EXPECT_EQ(db.check(), static_cast<std::size_t>(kCount));
    const auto all = db.scan("", "");
    ASSERT_EQ(all.size(), static_cast<std::size_t>(kCount));
    for (int i = 0; i < kCount; ++i) {
        EXPECT_EQ(all[static_cast<std::size_t>(i)].first, key_of(i));
    }
    const auto range = db.scan(key_of(100), key_of(110));
    ASSERT_EQ(range.size(), 10u);
    EXPECT_EQ(range.front().first, key_of(100));
    EXPECT_EQ(range.back().first, key_of(109));
    EXPECT_EQ(db.scan(key_of(5), "", 3).size(), 3u);
}

TEST(Db, MatchesStdMapUnderRandomOperations) {
    TempDir dir;
    const std::string path = dir.file("db");
    std::map<std::string, std::string> model;
    std::mt19937 rng(12345);
    {
        Db db(path, Options{24, 256u << 10});
        for (int step = 0; step < 10000; ++step) {
            const std::string key = key_of(static_cast<int>(rng() % 1500));
            const unsigned op = rng() % 10;
            if (op < 6) {
                const std::string value(rng() % (kMaxValueSize + 1), static_cast<char>('a' + rng() % 26));
                db.put(key, value);
                model[key] = value;
            } else if (op < 9) {
                EXPECT_EQ(db.del(key), model.erase(key) == 1);
            } else {
                const auto got = db.get(key);
                const auto it = model.find(key);
                ASSERT_EQ(got.has_value(), it != model.end());
                if (got) {
                    EXPECT_EQ(*got, it->second);
                }
            }
        }
        EXPECT_EQ(db.check(), model.size());
    }
    Db reopened(path);  // clean close and reopen: same contents
    const auto all = reopened.scan("", "");
    ASSERT_EQ(all.size(), model.size());
    auto it = model.begin();
    for (const auto& [k, v] : all) {
        EXPECT_EQ(k, it->first);
        EXPECT_EQ(v, it->second);
        ++it;
    }
}

TEST(Recovery, CommittedWritesSurviveWithoutCheckpoint) {
    TempDir dir;
    const std::string path = dir.file("db");
    {
        // A huge checkpoint threshold and no clean close: everything after open lives only
        // in the log and in the cache. Simulate the crash by copying the files before the
        // destructor runs its checkpoint.
        Db db(path, Options{64, 1u << 30});
        for (int i = 0; i < 500; ++i) {
            db.put(key_of(i), "value" + std::to_string(i));
        }
        std::filesystem::copy_file(path, path + ".crash");
        std::filesystem::copy_file(path + "-wal", path + ".crash-wal");
    }
    Db db(path + ".crash");
    EXPECT_GT(db.recovery_stats().committed_txns, 0u);
    EXPECT_EQ(db.check(), 500u);
    for (int i = 0; i < 500; ++i) {
        EXPECT_EQ(db.get(key_of(i)).value_or(""), "value" + std::to_string(i));
    }
}

namespace {

// Ends of the committed records in a log file, and the page ids they carry.
struct LogSummary {
    Lsn end_of_last_commit = 0;
    std::vector<PageId> pages;
};

LogSummary summarize_log(const std::string& wal_path) {
    LogSummary summary;
    Wal wal(wal_path);
    summary.end_of_last_commit = wal.start_lsn();
    wal.replay([&](const WalRecord& r) {
        if (r.type == RecordType::PageImage) {
            summary.pages.push_back(r.page_id);
        } else {
            summary.end_of_last_commit = r.lsn + Wal::kRecordHeaderSize + 8;
        }
    });
    return summary;
}

}  // namespace

TEST(Recovery, TornDataPageIsRepairedFromTheLog) {
    TempDir dir;
    const std::string path = dir.file("db");
    {
        Db db(path, Options{64, 1u << 30});
        for (int i = 0; i < 300; ++i) {
            db.put(key_of(i), "v");
        }
        db.checkpoint();                        // data file current, log empty
        db.put(key_of(0), "after-checkpoint");  // logged; the leaf is dirty only in the cache
        std::filesystem::copy_file(path, path + ".crash");
        std::filesystem::copy_file(path + "-wal", path + ".crash-wal");
    }
    const LogSummary log = summarize_log(path + ".crash-wal");
    ASSERT_FALSE(log.pages.empty());
    {
        // Tear the logged page in the copy: second half overwritten with garbage, as if the
        // power failed in the middle of the 4 KiB write.
        File f = File::open(path + ".crash", false);
        const std::string junk(kPageSize / 2, '\x7f');
        f.write_at(static_cast<std::uint64_t>(log.pages.front()) * kPageSize + kPageSize / 2, junk.data(),
                   junk.size());
    }
    Db db(path + ".crash");
    EXPECT_GE(db.recovery_stats().pages_redone, 1u);
    EXPECT_EQ(db.get(key_of(0)).value_or(""), "after-checkpoint");
    EXPECT_EQ(db.check(), 300u);
}

TEST(Recovery, UncommittedTailIsDiscardedAndNotReplayedLater) {
    TempDir dir;
    const std::string path = dir.file("db");
    {
        Db db(path, Options{64, 1u << 30});
        db.put("a", "1");
        std::filesystem::copy_file(path, path + ".crash");
        std::filesystem::copy_file(path + "-wal", path + ".crash-wal");
    }
    {
        // Append one page image with no commit record: a crash between append and commit.
        // The image is an empty leaf for the root page; applying it would wipe "a".
        const LogSummary log = summarize_log(path + ".crash-wal");
        Wal wal(path + ".crash-wal");
        wal.truncate_at(log.end_of_last_commit);
        Page empty_leaf = BPlusTree::initial_pages()[1];
        wal.append_page(1, empty_leaf);
        wal.sync();
    }
    {
        Db db(path + ".crash");
        EXPECT_EQ(db.recovery_stats().discarded_records, 1u);
        EXPECT_EQ(db.get("a").value_or(""), "1");
        db.put("b", "2");  // appended after the discarded tail was cut off
    }
    Db db(path + ".crash");
    EXPECT_EQ(db.get("a").value_or(""), "1");
    EXPECT_EQ(db.get("b").value_or(""), "2");
}

docs.text:
git add -A
git commit -m "Add Db, commit protocol, checkpoints and redo-only recovery


- Db: one mutex; every put/del is a transaction with the strong exception guarantee
- commit: append page images + commit record, fdatasync, then release pages (no-force)
- a failed fdatasync poisons the Db until reopen (fsyncgate)
- checkpoint: flush dirty pages, sync data file, reset the log; on open and on close
- Recovery: redo committed images in LSN order, skip current pages, discard the
  uncommitted tail and cut the log after the last commit
- LSN 0 reserved for never-logged pages (first record at LSN 1 was skipped by redo)
- tests: model test through the API, recovery without checkpoint, torn page repair,
  uncommitted tail discarded and not replayed later"
git push

docs.title: What to say in an interview
docs.text: "Every put is a transaction. Its changed pages are logged as full images plus a commit record, the log is fdatasynced once, and only then does the call return. The data file is written later, at eviction or checkpoint, always after the log record it depends on. Because uncommitted pages never reach the data file, recovery is redo-only: replay the log, apply committed page images, drop the uncommitted tail. Full images make redo idempotent and repair torn pages for free. Compared with ARIES I gave up steal, so a transaction's pages must fit in the cache, and in exchange I have no undo pass and no compensation records. And I can tell you about the bug where the first write of every database was lost because the first log record had the same LSN as a never-logged page."

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Prove the durability contract with a test that kills the process mid-write, add a CLI and a benchmark, make CI run everything under the sanitizers, and tag v0.1.0.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
The crash test is specified in 00_spec.md section 8. The design points to defend:

  • fork() plus SIGKILL, not an exception or exit(): SIGKILL cannot be caught, so no destructor, checkpoint or flush runs. That is a process crash, faithfully.
  • The pipe is the acknowledgement channel. The child writes i + 1 after operation i returns. The parent drains the pipe after the kill: everything the child wrote before dying is still there, and read returns 0 once the only write end has died.
  • Deterministic operations. Operation i is a pure function of i, so the parent rebuilds the expected state for any prefix with a std::map, without trusting the child.
  • acked or acked + 1. The operation in flight may have committed just before the kill, without its acknowledgement reaching the pipe. Anything else is a bug.
  • A small cache and a small checkpoint threshold in the child, so kills land during evictions and checkpoints, not only during commits.
  • The test must be able to fail. It also asserts that something was acknowledged, and it was checked against a mutant: with redo disabled in Recovery, it fails on the first kill (state matches neither 28 nor 29 operations). Do the same mutation on your version once.
  • What it does not test: power loss. After SIGKILL the kernel still writes its page cache to disk, so an engine that never called fdatasync would pass. Say so before you are asked, and name the tools that do test it (dm-log-writes, dm-flakey, LazyFS, VM snapshots).

docs.title: Files
docs.text: tests/crash_test.cpp, apps/minidb_cli.cpp, tools/bench.cpp, README.md, CI updates.

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
tests/crash_test.cpp:

// The crash test: a child process writes as fast as it can and reports every acknowledged
// operation through a pipe; the parent SIGKILLs it at a random moment, reopens the database
// and checks that the state equals the model after exactly the acknowledged operations
// (or after one more: the operation in flight may have committed just before the kill).
//
// SIGKILL cannot be caught, so no destructor, no checkpoint and no flush runs in the child.
// That is the same as a process crash. It is not the same as a power failure (the kernel
// still writes back the page cache); see the spec, section 8, for what that would take.

#include <signal.h>
#include <sys/wait.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include <cerrno>
#include <chrono>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <filesystem>
#include <map>
#include <random>
#include <string>
#include <thread>

#include <gtest/gtest.h>

#include "minidb/db.hpp"
#include "test_util.hpp"

using namespace minidb;

namespace {

constexpr int kKeySpace = 400;

std::string key_of(int i) {
    char buf[16];
    std::snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, "k%05d", i % kKeySpace);
    return buf;
}

// Operation i is a pure function of i, so the parent can recompute the expected state for
// any prefix of the operation sequence without talking to the child.
struct Op {
    bool is_delete = false;
    std::string key;
    std::string value;
};

Op op_at(std::uint32_t i) {
    Op op;
    op.key = key_of(static_cast<int>((i * 7u) % kKeySpace));
    op.is_delete = i % 11 == 10;
    if (!op.is_delete) {
        op.value = "v" + std::to_string(i) + ":" + std::string(i % 600, 'x');  // 0..~610 bytes
    }
    return op;
}

std::map<std::string, std::string> model_after(std::uint32_t count) {
    std::map<std::string, std::string> model;
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
        const Op op = op_at(i);
        if (op.is_delete) {
            model.erase(op.key);
        } else {
            model[op.key] = op.value;
        }
    }
    return model;
}

[[noreturn]] void child_main(const std::string& path, int ack_fd) {
    try {
        // Small cache and a small checkpoint threshold, so kills land during evictions and
        // during checkpoints, not only during commits.
        Db db(path, Options{16, 128u << 10});
        for (std::uint32_t i = 0;; ++i) {
            const Op op = op_at(i);
            if (op.is_delete) {
                db.del(op.key);
            } else {
                db.put(op.key, op.value);
            }
            // The acknowledgement: operation i returned, so it must survive any crash.
            const std::uint32_t done = i + 1;
            if (::write(ack_fd, &done, sizeof done) != static_cast<ssize_t>(sizeof done)) {
                ::_exit(3);
            }
        }
    } catch (...) {
        ::_exit(2);
    }
}

std::map<std::string, std::string> contents(Db& db) {
    std::map<std::string, std::string> out;
    for (auto& [k, v] : db.scan("", "")) {
        out.emplace(std::move(k), std::move(v));
    }
    return out;
}

}  // namespace

TEST(Crash, SigkillMidWriteLosesNoAcknowledgedOperation) {
    TempDir dir;
    const std::string path = dir.file("db");
    std::mt19937 rng(std::random_device{}());
    std::uint32_t total_acked = 0;

    for (int round = 0; round < 25; ++round) {
        // Every round starts from an empty database, so the expected state is simply the
        // model after the first `acked` operations.
        std::filesystem::remove(path);
        std::filesystem::remove(path + "-wal");

        int fds[2];
        ASSERT_EQ(::pipe(fds), 0);
        const pid_t pid = ::fork();
        ASSERT_GE(pid, 0);
        if (pid == 0) {
            ::close(fds[0]);
            child_main(path, fds[1]);  // never returns
        }
        ::close(fds[1]);

        // Let the child run for a random 20..200 ms, then kill it wherever it is.
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(20 + rng() % 180));
        ASSERT_EQ(::kill(pid, SIGKILL), 0);
        int status = 0;
        ASSERT_EQ(::waitpid(pid, &status, 0), pid);
        ASSERT_TRUE(WIFSIGNALED(status)) << "child exited early with status " << WEXITSTATUS(status);

        // Acknowledgements written before the kill are still in the pipe. read() returns 0
        // once they are drained, because the only write end died with the child.
        std::uint32_t acked = 0;
        std::uint32_t value = 0;
        while (::read(fds[0], &value, sizeof value) == static_cast<ssize_t>(sizeof value)) {
            acked = value;
        }
        ::close(fds[0]);

        Db db(path, Options{16, 128u << 10});  // runs recovery
        db.check();
        const auto actual = contents(db);
        EXPECT_TRUE(actual == model_after(acked) || actual == model_after(acked + 1))
            << "round " << round << ": state matches neither " << acked << " nor " << acked + 1
            << " operations (recovered " << db.recovery_stats().committed_txns << " txns, discarded "
            << db.recovery_stats().discarded_records << " records)";
        total_acked += acked;
        if (HasFailure()) {
            break;
        }
    }
    EXPECT_GT(total_acked, 0u) << "the child never acknowledged anything; the test proved nothing";
    std::printf("[ crash ] %u operations acknowledged across 25 kills\n", total_acked);
}

Notes on the code:

  • The child calls ::_exit, never exit, on its error paths: exit would run GoogleTest's and the parent's static destructors in the child, a classic fork bug.
  • fork is safe here because the test process is single-threaded at that point. Forking a multithreaded process copies only the calling thread, and any mutex another thread held stays locked forever in the child.
  • A run prints how much it proved, for example [ crash ] 1011 operations acknowledged across 25 kills (from one run of the reference code on WSL2; yours will differ). If that number is near zero, the kills are landing before the database even opens: raise the sleep range.

apps/minidb_cli.cpp, outlined (about 80 lines; you wrote tcpkv_cli already):

  • minidb_cli <file> <command> [args]; commands as in 00_spec.md section 3.2.
  • Open minidb::Db db(file); print db.recovery_stats() on stderr if it redid or discarded anything, so you can watch recovery happen after you kill -9 a writer.
  • put takes the rest of the command line as the value; get prints the value or (nil); scan prints key<TAB>value lines; check prints the key count or the CorruptionError message and exits 1; stats prints page count (meta), log size, cache hits/misses.
  • Catch std::invalid_argument (usage error, exit 2), minidb::CorruptionError (exit 3), std::exception (exit 1).

A manual crash demo for the README:

./build/release/minidb_cli /tmp/demo.db put greeting hello
( while true; do ./build/release/minidb_cli /tmp/demo.db put k$RANDOM v; done ) &
sleep 2; kill -9 %1
./build/release/minidb_cli /tmp/demo.db check     # recovery runs, then the checker

(kill -9 here hits the shell loop or one CLI process mid-write; either way the next open recovers.)

tools/bench.cpp, outlined: minidb_bench <file> <count> <value_size> times count puts with sequential keys, count puts with random keys, count gets, and one full scan, and prints operations per second for each. Expect puts to be bound by fdatasync latency, so the number mostly measures your disk (and WSL2's virtual disk), not the tree: say exactly that in the README, next to the numbers and the machine. The experiment worth adding: a second run with a WriteBatch of 100 puts per transaction (one sync per batch) shows how much group commit would buy.

CI: add crash to the test list (already in the CMakeLists.txt above) and keep the debug, release, asan, tsan, ubsan matrix from tcpkv. On the TSan job, apply the same vm.mmap_rnd_bits=28 step as tcpkv.

README: follow 00_spec.md section 10. The first screen must state the durability contract in one sentence and link to the crash test.

docs.title: What to say in an interview
docs.text: "The durability claim is tested, not asserted. A forked child writes as fast as it can and reports each acknowledged operation through a pipe; the parent kills it with SIGKILL at a random moment, reopens the database, which runs recovery, and checks that the contents equal a model after exactly the acknowledged operations, or one more for the operation in flight. It does that 25 times per run, under ASan and TSan too, and I checked that the test fails if I disable redo. What it does not cover is power loss, because after a process crash the kernel still flushes its page cache; for that I would use dm-log-writes or LazyFS to replay every prefix of the write stream."

docs.title: After v0.1.0: the resume line, and what next
docs.text:
Only once the tag exists, CI is green and the repository is public:

minidb — B+tree storage engine with write-ahead logging · C++17, Linux, CMake, GoogleTest · github.com/khanshaki-r/minidb - Page-based key-value store: 4 KiB checksummed pages, LRU buffer pool with no-steal/no-force policies, B+tree with byte-balanced splits and range scans, full-page-image WAL with LSNs, checkpoints, and redo-only crash recovery. - Crash test kills the writer with SIGKILL mid-operation 25 times per run and verifies that every acknowledged write survives and no unacknowledged one appears; runs under ASan, TSan and UBSan in CI.

Do not add a throughput number unless you measured it with the procedure from tcpkv step 10, and if you do, say that it is fsync-bound.

What next, in the order an interviewer would find most interesting (each is in 00_spec.md section 11): group commit; delta log records with a full image on first touch after a checkpoint; latch crabbing for concurrent readers; merges and a free list; power-loss testing.

docs.title: tcpkv specification
docs.text: Status: this is the contract. Every step builds a piece of it; code/ implements all of it. If a step and this document disagree, this document wins and the step has a bug.

docs.title: 1. In plain words
docs.text:
tcpkv is a program that listens on a TCP port, keeps a table of keys and values in memory, and lets many clients at once read and write that table by sending short text commands. Think of it as the smallest useful cousin of Redis: SET name shakir, GET name, done.

The point is not the feature list. The point is that every part of a real server is present and done properly: a wire protocol with limits and error handling, a store that is safe to share between threads, sockets wrapped so descriptors cannot leak, a pool of worker threads, a shutdown that does not lose or corrupt anything, tests for each piece, and a build that is warning-free and sanitizer-clean.

docs.title: 2. Goals and non-goals
docs.text:
Goals:

  • Correct under concurrent load: no data races, no torn values, no leaked descriptors or memory.
  • Small: one library, two executables, two tools, five test binaries. About 3,500 lines.
  • Everything explainable: no dependency except GoogleTest, no framework, no magic.

Non-goals (and things to say when asked "why not"):

  • Persistence. Memory only. (minidb is the persistence project.)
  • Replication, clustering, authentication, TLS.
  • Beating Redis on throughput. A thread-per-connection pool cannot; see INTERVIEW_TALKING_POINTS.md.

docs.title: 3.1 Design decision: text, line-based, length-prefixed values
docs.text:
Three options were considered for values that may contain spaces or newlines:

option pros cons quoting and escaping ("a b") readable in nc escaping is the classic source of parser bugs; O(n) rescans; still cannot carry arbitrary bytes without a second escape layer binary framing (fixed header) fastest to parse useless with nc/telnet; harder to debug by eye length prefix (SET k 5 hello ) binary-safe, O(1) to find the end, trivially pipelined, still typeable in nc the client must count bytes (the library does it)

Length prefix wins. It is what Redis's RESP does for bulk strings and for the same reasons. Commands themselves stay inline (GET key) because keys are restricted to printable ASCII without whitespace, so there is nothing to escape.

docs.title: 3.2 Grammar
docs.text:
request   := inline '\n'
           | "SET" SP key SP length '\n' bytes '\n'      ; bytes is exactly `length` octets
inline    := command { SP arg }                          ; blank lines are ignored
SP        := one or more ' ' or '\t'
EOL       := '\n' optionally preceded by '\r'
command   := PING | GET | SET | DEL | EXISTS | KEYS | EXPIRE | TTL | STATS | QUIT   (case-insensitive)
key       := 1..256 octets, each in 0x21..0x7E  (printable ASCII, no space)
prefix    := 0..256 octets, each in 0x21..0x7E
length    := decimal integer 0..1048576
seconds   := decimal integer, optional leading '-'

reply     := '+' text EOL                 ; status        (+PONG, +OK, +BYE)
           | "-ERR " text EOL             ; error
           | ':' integer EOL              ; integer (may be negative)
           | '$' length EOL bytes EOL     ; bulk string (binary safe)
           | "$-1" EOL                    ; null (key not found)
           | '*' count EOL { bulk }       ; array of bulk strings

The server always emits \n (never \r\n). It accepts either from clients.

docs.title: 3.3 Commands
docs.text: request reply notes PING +PONG GET key bulk value, or $-1 expired keys count as missing SET key len + value +OK overwrites; clears any TTL DEL key [key ...] :n number actually removed 1..64 keys EXISTS key [key ...] :n number present 1..64 keys KEYS [prefix] array of matching keys, sorted ascending empty prefix = all keys EXPIRE key seconds :1 if the key exists (TTL set), :0 otherwise seconds <= 0 deletes the key TTL key :s seconds left (rounded up), :-1 no TTL, :-2 missing STATS bulk string, name value\n per line see section 7 QUIT +BYE, then the server closes the connection

docs.title: 3.4 Errors
docs.text:
Non-fatal: the server replies -ERR ... and keeps the connection. The offending line is skipped.

  • unknown command 'NAME'
  • wrong number of arguments for NAME, NAME takes no arguments
  • invalid key, invalid prefix, invalid value length, invalid expire seconds
  • too many arguments (more than 64 arguments)

Fatal: the server replies -ERR ... and closes the connection. After these, the server cannot know where the next request begins, so the only safe action is to hang up.

  • value too large (declared length > 1 MiB)
  • line too long (4096 bytes received without a newline)
  • value not terminated by newline (the byte after the value is neither \n nor \r\n)

docs.title: 3.5 Limits
docs.text: limit value reason key length 1..256 B keys are hashed and copied often; 256 is generous for type:id style keys value length 0..1 MiB bounds per-connection memory to a few MiB; larger blobs belong in a different system line length 4096 B 64 keys of 60 bytes fits; stops a client from growing our buffer forever arguments 64 caps the per-line work for DEL/EXISTS pipelining unbounded the parser is incremental; replies are batched per read()

docs.title: 3.6 Session example
docs.text:
C: SET greeting 11
C: hello world
S: +OK
C: GET greeting
S: $11
S: hello world
C: GET missing
S: $-1
C: DEL greeting missing
S: :1
C: FOO
S: -ERR unknown command 'FOO'
C: QUIT
S: +BYE

docs.title: 4. Architecture
docs.text:
main thread                          worker threads (fixed pool, N)
 +-------------------------------+     +----------------------------------------------+
 | tcpkv_server                  |     | Connection::serve()                          |
 |  parse flags                  |     |   loop:                                      |
 |  Store, Metrics, Server       |     |     if stop flag set: break                  |
 |  sigaction(SIGINT, SIGTERM)   |     |     poll(fd, 250 ms) ; timeout -> continue   |
 |  server.run():                |     |     n = read()      ; 0 -> peer closed       |
 |   ThreadPool pool(N)          |     |     parser.feed(buf, n)                      |
 |   loop:                       |     |     while parser.next(): execute -> out      |
 |     poll(listener, wake_pipe) |     |     write_all(out)                           |
 |     accept4()                 |     |   Socket destructor closes the fd            |
 |     Connection c{Socket,...}  |     +----------------------------------------------+
 |     pool.submit(move(c))      |                       |
 |     every 1 s: purge_expired  |                       v
 |     every 10 s: log ops/s     |          Store: unordered_map + shared_mutex
 |   ~ThreadPool: stop + join    |          Metrics: atomics + latency histogram
 +-------------------------------+
   signal handler: server.request_stop()  = atomic store + write(wake_pipe)

docs.title: 4.1 Components
docs.text: component header responsibility FileDescriptor fd.hpp owns one descriptor; closes exactly once; move-only Socket socket.hpp listen/connect/accept/read/write/poll with EINTR and partial-write handling; move-only Parser protocol.hpp incremental request parser (state machine); request and reply encoders; limits Store store.hpp unordered_map behind a shared_mutex; lazy expiry + periodic purge ThreadPool thread_pool.hpp N workers, one FIFO queue, MoveOnlyFunction tasks, drain/stop semantics Connection connection.hpp one client's session; move-only; owns the Socket; execute_command Server server.hpp acceptor loop, wake pipe, submits Connections, periodic maintenance Client client.hpp blocking client library; reply parser Metrics metrics.hpp atomic counters and a lock-free latency histogram log log.hpp levelled, thread-safe stderr logging

docs.title: 4.2 Threading model
docs.text:
• One acceptor thread (the thread that called Server::run).
  • N worker threads created once. A connection occupies one worker for its whole lifetime. N therefore bounds concurrent connections; connections beyond N wait in the pool queue (bounded by max_pending_connections, default 1024; beyond that: -ERR server busy, close).
  • Shared state: the Store (shared_mutex), Metrics (atomics), the stop flag (atomic), the pool queue (mutex + condition variables). Nothing else is shared.
  • Workers never block on each other except at the store lock. Writers hold the exclusive lock for one hash-map operation; readers run in parallel.

docs.title: 4.3 Ownership and lifetimes
docs.text:
• Store and Metrics outlive Server; Server outlives its ThreadPool; the pool outlives every Connection it runs. All of this is enforced by scope in main and run().
  • A Connection is created on the acceptor thread, moved into a lambda, moved into the queue, moved out by a worker. The Socket travels with it. Nothing is copied; nothing is shared; the descriptor closes when the lambda is destroyed, on whichever thread that is.
  • A queued connection that is never served (shutdown) is destroyed by ThreadPool::stop() outside the pool lock, which closes its socket.

docs.title: 4.4 Shutdown sequence
docs.text:
1. SIGINT/SIGTERM -> handler -> Server::request_stop(): stop_ = true, one byte to the wake pipe.
  2. The acceptor's poll() returns; the loop condition fails; it logs and leaves run().
  3. Leaving run() destroys the ThreadPool: stop() marks it stopped, drops queued connections (closing their sockets), wakes idle workers.
  4. Each busy worker's Connection::serve() sees stop_ within one poll interval (250 ms by default), finishes the write it was doing, shuts down its socket and returns.
  5. ~ThreadPool joins all workers. run() returns. main returns 0.

No command is half-applied: the store lock makes each operation atomic, and a worker that has read a command executes it and writes the reply before checking the flag again.

docs.title: 5. Non-functional requirements
docs.text: requirement how it is met how it is checked -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wshadow -Werror clean one tcpkv_warnings INTERFACE target linked by every binary every CI job no leaks, no invalid accesses RAII for every resource; no raw new/close ASan+LSan job; valgrind_check.sh under load_gen no data races shared_mutex, atomics, pool mutex; nothing else shared TSan job running the stress and integration tests no undefined behaviour memcpy for sockaddr casts, from_chars for integers, bounds checks on every buffer UBSan job graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM self-pipe + atomic flag + bounded poll ServerShutdown.* tests; manual Ctrl-C under Valgrind configurable port and thread count --port, --threads, --host, --idle-timeout, --max-pending, --stats-interval, --log-level --help; integration tests use port 0 robust to bad clients limits + fatal/non-fatal error split; MSG_NOSIGNAL; EINTR retries; partial writes protocol_test malformed cases; integration tests observable STATS command; periodic ops/s + p99 log line StatsReportsCounters test

docs.title: 6. Testing strategy
docs.text:
Four layers, each catching what the one below cannot.

  1. Unit tests without I/O. Parser, encoders, Store, ThreadPool, MoveOnlyFunction, execute_command. Fast, deterministic, run under every sanitizer. Malformed input is a first-class test subject: every error message in section 3.4 has a test.
  2. Unit tests with real descriptors. FileDescriptor (does the kernel agree it is closed?), Socket over loopback on an ephemeral port (echo, EOF, timeout, 4 MiB write that forces partial sends).
  3. Integration tests. A real Server on port 0 in a thread, real Clients and raw sockets. Pipelining, fatal errors, 16 clients on 4 workers, shutdown latency, active connection accounting.
  4. System tests. load_gen (C++ and Python) hammering the server while it runs under Valgrind in CI; TSan and ASan runs of the full test suite. load_gen verifies every GET, so it is a correctness check, not just a benchmark.

Thread-safety tests cannot prove the absence of races; TSan can prove the presence. So the stress tests are written to maximise interleavings (many threads, small key space, no sleeps) and the TSan preset is a required CI job.

docs.title: 7. Observability
docs.text:
STATS returns, one per line: uptime_seconds, connections_accepted, connections_active, connections_rejected, commands_total, commands_failed, bytes_in, bytes_out, latency_count, latency_mean_us, latency_p50_us, latency_p99_us, latency_p999_us.

Latency here is server-side execution time of the store operation (bucketed, log scale, 50 us to 5 s). Client-observed round trip is measured by load_gen.

Every 10 seconds (configurable) the acceptor logs: stats: 48213 commands in last 10 s (4821 ops/s), active connections 8, p99 100 us.

Log format: 2026-11-03T10:00:00.123 INFO [tid 4242] message on stderr; levels debug, info, warn, error; per-connection events at debug.

docs.text:
tcpkv/
  CMakeLists.txt              library + apps + tools + tests; warnings target; sanitizer option
  CMakePresets.json           debug, release, relwithdebinfo, asan, tsan, ubsan
  .github/workflows/ci.yml    matrix over presets + valgrind job + advisory clang-format
  .clang-format  .gitignore  LICENSE (MIT)  README.md
  docs/PROTOCOL.md
  include/tcpkv/              fd.hpp socket.hpp protocol.hpp store.hpp thread_pool.hpp
                              connection.hpp server.hpp client.hpp metrics.hpp log.hpp
  src/                        one .cpp per header
  apps/                       tcpkv_server.cpp  tcpkv_cli.cpp
  tools/                      load_gen.cpp  load_gen.py  valgrind_check.sh
  tests/                      fd_test.cpp protocol_test.cpp store_test.cpp thread_pool_test.cpp integration_test.cpp

docs.text:
1. Title, badges (CI, license, C++17, Linux), one-paragraph description, a 10-line demo session.

docs.title: 10. Licence
docs.text: MIT. It is the licence reviewers expect on a portfolio project, it lets anyone read, copy and learn from the code, and it has no obligations that could complicate a future employer's view of it. The copyright line uses your name and GitHub handle; replace it with your legal name before tagging if you prefer.

docs.title: Step 01. Project skeleton, CMake, CI with a hello test
docs.text: Time: ~5 hours Week: 1 (Oct 6 – Oct 12) Read first: 06_Linux_Toolchain_DevOps (CMake basics, Ninja, GitHub Actions, git workflow). Nothing from the C++ courses is needed yet.

docs.title: 1. Goal
docs.text:
At the end of this step there is a public GitHub repository with a CMake project that builds one GoogleTest binary, a CMakePresets.json so every build is one command, and a GitHub Actions workflow that turns green. No tcpkv code yet. The point is that from the very first commit the repo has the shape and the tooling of the finished product, so every later step is "add a file and a test", never "set up infrastructure".

In plain words: you are building the factory before the first car.

docs.title: 2. Set up the machine (WSL Ubuntu 24.04)
docs.text:
sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y build-essential g++ cmake ninja-build git valgrind clang-format gdb python3
g++ --version      # 13.x
cmake --version    # 3.28.x
ninja --version    # 1.11.x

Configure git once:

git config --global user.name "Shakir"
git config --global user.email "<the email on your GitHub account>"
git config --global init.defaultBranch main

Create the repository on GitHub first (web UI): name tcpkv, public, no README, no licence, no .gitignore (we add our own). Then:

mkdir -p ~/src/tcpkv && cd ~/src/tcpkv
git init
git remote add origin git@github.com:khanshaki-r/tcpkv.git

Set up an SSH key if you have not (ssh-keygen -t ed25519, add the public key in GitHub settings). HTTPS with a token also works.

docs.title: CMakeLists.txt
docs.text:
This is the step-01 version. Later steps add the library and executables; the structure stays.

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.22)

project(tcpkv
    VERSION 0.1.0
    DESCRIPTION "Multithreaded TCP key-value server"
    LANGUAGES CXX)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Language and build type
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)          # -std=c++17, not -std=gnu++17
set(CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS ON)  # compile_commands.json for clangd / clang-tidy

if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE AND NOT CMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TYPES)
    set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Debug CACHE STRING "Build type" FORCE)
endif()

option(TCPKV_BUILD_TESTS "Build the GoogleTest suite" ON)
set(TCPKV_SANITIZER "" CACHE STRING "Sanitizer to enable: address | thread | undefined | (empty)")

find_package(Threads REQUIRED)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Warnings: one INTERFACE target so every binary gets exactly the same flags
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
add_library(tcpkv_warnings INTERFACE)
target_compile_options(tcpkv_warnings INTERFACE
    -Wall
    -Wextra
    -Wpedantic
    -Wshadow
    -Wnon-virtual-dtor
    -Woverloaded-virtual
    -Werror)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sanitizers: applied to everything in this directory tree so library, tests and gtest agree
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
if(TCPKV_SANITIZER)
    message(STATUS "tcpkv: building with -fsanitize=${TCPKV_SANITIZER}")
    add_compile_options(-fsanitize=${TCPKV_SANITIZER} -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g)
    add_link_options(-fsanitize=${TCPKV_SANITIZER})
endif()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
if(TCPKV_BUILD_TESTS)
    include(FetchContent)
    FetchContent_Declare(
        googletest
        GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/google/googletest.git
        GIT_TAG        v1.14.0
        GIT_SHALLOW    TRUE)
    set(INSTALL_GTEST OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
    set(gtest_force_shared_crt ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
    FetchContent_MakeAvailable(googletest)

    enable_testing()
    include(GoogleTest)

    add_executable(hello_test tests/hello_test.cpp)
    target_link_libraries(hello_test PRIVATE GTest::gtest_main tcpkv_warnings Threads::Threads)
    gtest_discover_tests(hello_test DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT 120 PROPERTIES TIMEOUT 300)
endif()

Why each piece:

  • CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF gives -std=c++17 rather than -std=gnu++17. You want the standard language; the GNU extensions you need (like pipe2, accept4) come from glibc headers, which g++ enables anyway by defining _GNU_SOURCE.
  • The warnings are on an INTERFACE library instead of add_compile_options so that GoogleTest's own sources are not built with -Werror. Third-party code you do not control must never be able to break your build.
  • Sanitizers are applied globally (add_compile_options) because an instrumented test linked against an uninstrumented gtest, or vice versa, gives false positives.
  • FetchContent with a pinned tag: reproducible builds, no system package needed, works identically in CI.
  • gtest_discover_tests registers every TEST() as its own ctest entry, so a failure names the test, and ctest can run them in parallel.

docs.title: CMakePresets.json
docs.text:
This is the final version; it does not change later. A preset is a named bundle of generator + build directory + cache variables, so "build with TSan" is one command for you and for CI.

{
  "version": 6,
  "cmakeMinimumRequired": { "major": 3, "minor": 25, "patch": 0 },
  "configurePresets": [
    {
      "name": "base",
      "hidden": true,
      "generator": "Ninja",
      "binaryDir": "${sourceDir}/build/${presetName}",
      "cacheVariables": {
        "CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS": "ON"
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "debug",
      "displayName": "Debug",
      "inherits": "base",
      "cacheVariables": { "CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE": "Debug" }
    },
    {
      "name": "release",
      "displayName": "Release (-O3, no debug info)",
      "inherits": "base",
      "cacheVariables": { "CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE": "Release" }
    },
    {
      "name": "relwithdebinfo",
      "displayName": "RelWithDebInfo (for Valgrind and perf)",
      "inherits": "base",
      "cacheVariables": { "CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE": "RelWithDebInfo" }
    },
    {
      "name": "asan",
      "displayName": "AddressSanitizer + LeakSanitizer",
      "inherits": "base",
      "cacheVariables": {
        "CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE": "Debug",
        "TCPKV_SANITIZER": "address"
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "tsan",
      "displayName": "ThreadSanitizer",
      "inherits": "base",
      "cacheVariables": {
        "CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE": "RelWithDebInfo",
        "TCPKV_SANITIZER": "thread"
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "ubsan",
      "displayName": "UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer",
      "inherits": "base",
      "cacheVariables": {
        "CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE": "Debug",
        "TCPKV_SANITIZER": "undefined"
      }
    }
  ],
  "buildPresets": [
    { "name": "debug", "configurePreset": "debug" },
    { "name": "release", "configurePreset": "release" },
    { "name": "relwithdebinfo", "configurePreset": "relwithdebinfo" },
    { "name": "asan", "configurePreset": "asan" },
    { "name": "tsan", "configurePreset": "tsan" },
    { "name": "ubsan", "configurePreset": "ubsan" }
  ],
  "testPresets": [
    {
      "name": "base-test",
      "hidden": true,
      "output": { "outputOnFailure": true },
      "execution": { "noTestsAction": "error", "stopOnFailure": false }
    },
    { "name": "debug", "inherits": "base-test", "configurePreset": "debug" },
    { "name": "release", "inherits": "base-test", "configurePreset": "release" },
    { "name": "relwithdebinfo", "inherits": "base-test", "configurePreset": "relwithdebinfo" },
    {
      "name": "asan",
      "inherits": "base-test",
      "configurePreset": "asan",
      "environment": { "ASAN_OPTIONS": "detect_leaks=1:halt_on_error=1:strict_string_checks=1" }
    },
    {
      "name": "tsan",
      "inherits": "base-test",
      "configurePreset": "tsan",
      "environment": { "TSAN_OPTIONS": "halt_on_error=1:second_deadlock_stack=1" }
    },
    {
      "name": "ubsan",
      "inherits": "base-test",
      "configurePreset": "ubsan",
      "environment": { "UBSAN_OPTIONS": "halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=1" }
    }
  ]
}

TSan uses RelWithDebInfo because TSan on an unoptimised build is painfully slow and the compiler at -O0 keeps values in memory in ways that produce no false positives but a lot of noise in timing-sensitive tests.

docs.title: tests/hello_test.cpp
docs.text:
A throwaway. It exists so the whole chain (configure, fetch gtest, build, discover, run, CI) is proven before any real code exists. Step 02 deletes it.

#include <utility>

#include <gtest/gtest.h>

TEST(Hello, ToolchainWorks) {
    EXPECT_EQ(1 + 1, 2);
}

TEST(Hello, Cpp17IsEnabled) {
    // Structured bindings are C++17; this fails to compile on an older standard.
    const auto [a, b] = std::pair<int, int>{1, 2};
    EXPECT_EQ(a + b, 3);
}

docs.title: .github/workflows/ci.yml
docs.text:
Step-01 version: debug and asan only. Step 08 extends it to the full matrix plus Valgrind.

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  build-and-test:
    name: ${{ matrix.preset }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        preset: [debug, asan]
    steps:

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4


      - name: Install toolchain
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ninja-build g++


      - name: Configure
        run: cmake --preset ${{ matrix.preset }}


      - name: Build
        run: cmake --build --preset ${{ matrix.preset }} --parallel


      - name: Test
        run: ctest --preset ${{ matrix.preset }} --parallel 2

ubuntu-24.04 is the same OS as your WSL, so "works on my machine" and "works in CI" mean the same compiler and the same glibc.
